topicName: App Store and Google Play Preparation
content: [{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"App Store and Google Play Preparation in NativeScript"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Preparing your NativeScript application for submission to the Apple App Store and Google Play Store is a crucial final step. This guide covers the essential configurations, asset generation, and build commands required to successfully publish your cross-platform mobile app."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"1. Configuring Application Metadata and Icons"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"Before building your application for production, you must configure your app's display name, version, bundle identifier, and icons. These are primarily managed in the App_Resources folder and package.json."},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Bundle Identifier: Ensure your app has a unique identifier like \"com.company.appname\" set in your native configuration files."},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"App Icons: Use the NativeScript Image Assets generator or CLI tools to generate icons for both iOS and Android platforms across all required resolutions."},{"order":7,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Splash Screens: Configure launch screens in App_Resources to provide a seamless startup experience."},{"order":8,"type":"subheading","text":"2. Preparing for iOS (Apple App Store)"},{"order":9,"type":"paragraph","text":"To build and release your NativeScript app for iOS, you need an active Apple Developer account, a valid provisioning profile, and a distribution certificate. You can build the release package using the NativeScript CLI."},{"order":10,"type":"code","text":"ns build ios --release --env.appleTeamId=YOUR_TEAM_ID"},{"order":11,"type":"paragraph","text":"Once the build is complete, open the generated Xcode project located in platforms/ios to archive and upload your app via Xcode Organizer or Transporter."},{"order":12,"type":"subheading","text":"3. Preparing for Android (Google Play Store)"},{"order":13,"type":"paragraph","text":"For Android, you must generate a release-ready Android App Bundle (.aab). Google Play requires all new apps to be submitted in the AAB format. First, generate a signing keystore if you haven't already."},{"order":14,"type":"code","text":"keytool -genkey -v -keystore my-release-key.jks -keyalg RSA -keysize 2048 -validity 10000 -alias my-alias"},{"order":15,"type":"paragraph","text":"Configure your release keystore credentials inside the App_Resources/Android/app.gradle file or via environment variables, then execute the release build command."},{"order":16,"type":"code","text":"ns build android --release --env.licenseAgreement"},{"order":17,"type":"subheading","text":"4. Final Verification and Testing"},{"order":18,"type":"paragraph","text":"Before submitting your binaries to the respective stores, thoroughly test the release builds on physical devices. Release builds often enable code obfuscation, minification, and strict security policies that may affect third-party plugins. Always test push notifications, in-app purchases, and backend API connections thoroughly."}]
